Check derivatives against finite differences

Source: R/test_util.R
test_util_check_grads.Rd

Ports of jax.test_util.check_grads, check_jvp and check_vjp. Derivatives are compared with a central finite difference in one random direction, so the cost does not grow with the number of inputs or outputs. test_util_check_grads() checks forward and reverse mode up to order.

Usage

test_util_check_grads(
  f,
  args,
  order,
  modes = c("fwd", "rev"),
  atol = NULL,
  rtol = NULL,
  eps = NULL
)

test_util_check_jvp(
  f,
  f_jvp,
  args,
  atol = NULL,
  rtol = NULL,
  eps = 1e-04,
  err_msg = ""
)

test_util_check_vjp(
  f,
  f_vjp,
  args,
  atol = NULL,
  rtol = NULL,
  eps = 1e-04,
  err_msg = ""
)

Arguments

f

Function to check at do.call(f, args).

args

List of argument values.

order

Derivatives up to this order are checked.

modes

Modes to check: any of "fwd", "rev" and "lin".

atol, rtol

Absolute and relative tolerance.

eps

Step of the finite difference (default 1e-4).

f_jvp

Function of (primals, tangents) computing the JVP of f, typically function(p, t) jvp(f, p, t).

err_msg

Text added to the error message.

f_vjp

Function of the arguments computing the VJP of f, typically function(...) vjp(f, ...).

Value

TRUE, invisibly; an error of class jax_assertion_error when a check fails.

Details

Tolerances default to JAX's per dtype gradient tolerances (2e-3 for float32, 1e-5 for float64); as in JAX they are multiplied by the number of elements compared. Pass one number, or numbers named by dtype to override single dtypes. The random direction is drawn with a fixed seed and the caller's random number stream is left untouched.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
test_util_check_grads(function(x) sin(x) * x, list(as_jax(c(1, 2, 3))), order = 2)
} # }
